glasgow_cathedral_verger.text: Welcome to Glasgow Cathedral, also called the High Kirk of Glasgow or St Mungo's. Quiet feet, please. The stones echo.
Most of what you see went up in the 1200s. It is the only medieval cathedral on the Scottish mainland to come through the Reformation with its roof on.
St Mungo, the city's patron saint, is buried in the lower church, among a forest of stone pillars. Pilgrims have come to his tomb for centuries.

glasgow_cathedral_visitor.text: The ring in the fish is the best bit of Mungo's story. A queen lost her ring, and it turned up inside a salmon. That is why the city's coat of arms has a fish with a ring.
The Necropolis is next door, a hill of Victorian graves and statues. Spooky? Not really. Mostly it has very good views.

then.text: Thank you for asking about him. Hardly anyone says his name now. I like it when they do.

else.text: My husband used to bring me here on Sundays. It's eight months now. People keep telling me it gets easier. It doesn't, quite. It gets different.

options: I'm sorry. Tell me about him

then.text: She smiles properly for the first time. 'Duncan. He whistled out of tune all through the Hallelujah Chorus.' You listen to a whole marriage in ten minutes.
She nods politely. People mean well. Lines like that tend to close the conversation, where a name opens it.
She laughs, to her own surprise. 'I took up the oboe. The neighbours have views.'

else.text: There's no timetable for grief, and no tidy stages you pass through in order. Some days are fine, and then a song in a shop undoes you.
Saying their name helps. It's usually the silence that hurts, not the mention.
If it feels too heavy, your GP can help, and Cruse Bereavement Support has a free helpline on 0808 808 1677. Now sit a minute. Have a cuppa.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
